content:
Aisha Bello: heads up: burn-rate alerts are *way* noisier than expected since yesterday’s rule rollout. overnight we had ~60 pages in platform-oncall, most were <5 min blips + same underlying issue but split by model/route.

Rafael Mendes: yeah saw that. a bunch were `Hosted / us-east-1 / chat_stream / llama-3.1-70b` + same for `…-8b` etc. not actionable to page 6 times for the same gateway hiccup.

Sergio Costa: confirming: current alert labels include `tier, region, route, model, status_class` and the notification grouping is basically none (pager sees each unique labelset). We used the template from observability-pack PR but didn’t add group_by in Alertmanager yet.

Allison Grant: a few things to fix:
1) alertmanager grouping (group_by + group_wait/group_interval)
2) thresholds — we’re paging on 2x burn for 5m/1h which is super sensitive
3) low-traffic series: burn math gets spiky when denominator is tiny

Sean Gallagher: +1. goal is “feel” budget burn, not “page on every transient.” we need multi-window burn alerts per the standard, but w/ sane sensitivity per tier.

Nadia Rahman: looking at raw data: for some models the request volume drops to single digits overnight. One timeout => error rate jumps and burn calculation goes nuts. We should either (a) use a min request threshold in the SLI query or (b) aggregate across models for paging.

Thomas Baird: the cardinality is already painful. If we keep paging per-model we’ll be in trouble anyway. I’d strongly prefer page on `{tier, region, route, service}` and keep per-model breakdown as dashboard-only.

Amara Diallo: from gateway side: a lot of the “burn” last night was short-lived 499 spikes (client aborts) during a partner load test. Those shouldn’t page at the same level as 5xx/timeouts. are we counting 499 as failures in the burn SLI right now?

Aisha Bello: currently: burn SLI uses “request success” = HTTP <500 AND not timeout. 499 is treated as success (but the streaming disconnect alert is separate and is paging too). The pages I saw were mostly `timeout_rate` + `disconnect_rate`.

Miles Thornton: disconnect pages were brutal. We had disconnect burn alerts firing for both `ttft` and `stream_duration` panels (?) feels like we’re double-counting symptoms.

Sergio Costa: yeah we set up two alerts:
- `burn_streaming_disconnect_rate` (5m/1h, 30m/6h)
- `burn_streaming_latency_ttft` (same windows)
So when a region has issues you get 2x alerts per labelset.

Allison Grant: recommendation (matches our burn-rate standard):
- page only on “fast burn” (e.g. 5m/1h) at high threshold, ticket on “slow burn” (e.g. 30m/6h)
- use two-window *AND* semantics to avoid blips
- tune thresholds by tier: Hosted can tolerate more burstiness than Dedicated

Rafael Mendes: can we propose concrete numbers?
For Hosted: page if (5m/1h) > 14x AND (30m/6h) > 6x. ticket if (2h/24h) > 3x.
For Dedicated: page if (5m/1h) > 8x AND (30m/6h) > 4x. (lower because customers notice immediately)

Sean Gallagher: i like that direction. also: group alerts so one incident => one page per tier+region+route. model-level goes in the alert *annotations* as “top contributors”.

Nadia Rahman: +1 “top contributors” based on error counts in the window, not rates. Otherwise low-traffic models dominate.

Thomas Baird: +1000. Also please drop `status_class` from labels for burn alerts. It multiplies series and creates separate pages (timeout vs 5xx vs disconnect). We can keep it in the dashboard.

Amara Diallo: + add a “maintenance / load test” switch? Not forever, but for partner tests we need a way to silence without deleting rules.

Aisha Bello: we can do silence, but i’d rather not rely on humans. If we add min volume thresholds it’ll also help with load tests that only touch a subset.

Sergio Costa: Implementation sketch:
- Update alert rules to aggregate over `model` for paging alerts (`sum by (tier, region, route, service)`)
- Add `min_requests` guard in recording rules (e.g. only compute burn where req_count_5m >= 200 for Hosted)
- Configure Alertmanager: `group_by: [alertname, tier, region, route, service]`, group_wait 2m, group_interval 10m, repeat_interval 2h

Allison Grant: careful with hardcoding 200. for embeddings routes volume is lower. maybe make it per-route via config or use “min tokens” for streaming?

Rafael Mendes: for MVP we can do:
- chat/completions streaming: min_requests_5m = 200
- non-streaming completions: 100
- embeddings: 50
and revisit after backtest.

Incident Bot: (from last night) 03:12-03:27 UTC: "Hosted burn-rate alert storm" detected. Top alerts: burn_streaming_disconnect_rate (us-east-1), burn_timeout_rate (us-east-1). Linked dashboards: https://console.redwoodinference.com/d/slo-hosted-us-east-1 (internal)

Miles Thornton: also: should disconnect alerts be ticket-only unless it’s server-side disconnect? client aborts happen.

Aisha Bello: we already separate `client_abort` vs `server_disconnect` in the new gateway metrics, but the alert query is still using the old `disconnect_total` (all reasons). We should switch to paging only on server-side disconnect burn. Client abort burn => ticket.

Sean Gallagher: great. action items:
- Sergio: update Alertmanager grouping + rule labelsets (drop model/status_class for paging) + add annotation for top models (by errors)
- Aisha/Nadia: propose min-volume guards per route + validate against last 2 weeks
- Allison: sanity check thresholds vs org burn-rate standard, especially for Dedicated
- Amara: confirm new disconnect reason metric is stable and available in all regions
Target: have a tuned ruleset ready for end of week so oncall isn’t miserable.

Sergio Costa: ack. I’ll put up a PR in observability-pack today and a config change for Alertmanager. will post diff in this thread.

Allison Grant: once the PR is up, tag me + Rafael. I’ll also add a short note to the standard doc: “page alerts should not be per-model” (we keep learning this the hard way).

Rafael Mendes: thanks. also, can we flip paging to ticket-only until grouping lands? or set a temporary silence for `burn_streaming_disconnect_rate`?

Sean Gallagher: do a temporary silence for the disconnect page alert for 12h, but keep ticketing. don’t want to miss a real server-side regression.

Aisha Bello: done. silence set for `burn_streaming_disconnect_rate` paging rule until 18:00 UTC, ticket rule still active. :thumbsup:
